messages.body_plain:
On Tue, 29 Jun 2021 at 17:30, Richard Kuhlmeijer <r.kuhl...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thankyou! I managed to get the run the simulation all the different scenarios, but I also want each scenario (of the 45) to run 10 times. Previously I used this code in order to do so:
>
> env <- lapply(1:10, function(i) {

> ...

> })
>
> But now that gives the following error when running envs %>% get_mon_arrivals():
>
> Error in (function (x)  : unused argument (<environment>)

Note that, with lapply inside lapply/mclapply, you are generating a list of lists of environments, not a list of environments, which is what get_mon_arrivals is able to manage. So you either lapply get_mon_arrivals too or you need to unnest one level.

>
> }) #I used mc.cores=1 since windows doesn’t allow it to be >1

Then you are not parallelizing, and it's the same as using plain lapply. So for Windows, I recommend looking into future_lapply, from package future.apply. You can set plan(multisession), which should work on Windows too.

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Combining trajectories
messages.body_plain:
On Tue, 29 Jun 2021 at 17:25, Joe Micoud <de-w...@web.de> wrote:
>
> Great, the hint using simulate function works well.
>
> I would like to minimise total duration under possible ranges for resources and interarrival times. Thus, optimisation of allocation of resources, capacity rates and interarrival time. And in the end consideration/minimisation of budget as well.

simmer.optim is still experimental, but I believe it should work for you. Take a look at the example in the README. You can parametrize your variables (resources, interarrival times...) with .opt(), define your objective (total duration, or e.g. total duration * budget) and a set of constraints (e.g. for the budget), then apply different optimizers.

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.body_plain:
On Sat, 10 Jul 2021 at 04:52, Ralph Asher <ralph....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> (Hiding the actual context of the simulation)
>
> Let's say that we have a variant on the bank simulation.  Single queue, multiple servers, and for a given customer, each server will take the same amount of time on that customer. (e.g., customer A will take 3 minutes no matter which server; customer B will take 8 minutes).
>
> Here's the twist.  The tellers are so far apart from each other, that there is an appreciable travel time differential; and that travel time differential VARIES BY CUSTOMER.

This makes each teller different, so a single queue with multiple
servers is not enough anymore. You need an additional resource per
teller (with no queue, as the first resource is already controlling
the access) so that arrivals can select() the proper one according to
their distance, as well as an additional timeout to model that travel
time.

Iñaki

> So for example,
> Customer A to Teller #1 = 3 minutes walk.
> Customer A to Teller #2 = 10 minutes walk.
>
> Customer B to Teller #1 = 7 minutes walk.
> Customer B to Teller #2 = 6 minutes walk.
>
> {Yes, this loses its actual comparison to the physical world}
>
> I want to include logic where the Customer seizes the closest available teller, at the time of demand.  I can include this "travel time" into the customer service time, but only if I can list a different service time (or, potentially, just list it as a travel time) for each customer/server permutation.
>
> I haven't actually started coding yet, but haven't encountered this anywhere using The Google so wanted to see if I'm missing something big here.
>
> Thanks
> Ralph

messages.body_plain:
On Fri, 30 Jul 2021 at 05:26, martin wall <marti...@health.govt.nz> wrote:
> I am receiving an error message I don't understand when trying to use the 'schedule' function in the add_resource function
>
> > AirAmbulance_c %>%
>      add_resource("helicopter_shift_d", schedule(c(8, 16, 24), c(3, 2, 1), period=24)) %>%               add_generator("Call out", incident2, function() {c(0, rpois(99, 1.5), -1)})
> Error: resource 'helicopter_shift_d' was defined, but no schedule was attached In addition: Warning messages: 1: In add_resource_(.env$sim_obj, i, positive(capacity), positive(queue_size), : resource 'helicopter_shift_d' already defined 2: In add_resource_manager_(.env$sim_obj, i, "capacity", positive(capacity), : process 'helicopter_shift_d_capacity' already defined
>
> First it says that no schedule was attached and then that 'helicopter_shift_d_capacity is already defined

TL;DR, your simulation environment, at that point, already has a helicopter_shift_d resource defined. This usually happens when you are trying things interactively and you didn't clear the simulation environment properly. This is what happens:
We try to add a resource, but it already exists -> generates a warning.
We try to add the schedule, but it already exists -> generates a warning.
The schedule didn't succeed -> generates the error.
We could in theory avoid the last error, but we need protection against other kind of errors that could leave a resource without capacity defined.

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] add resource
messages.body_plain:
The simplest way is to instantiate a new simulator for each iteration. I tend to encapsulate the whole simulation in a simulate() function, and then run lapply for different seeds and/or different parameters. This is how it is done in [1], and discussed in [2]. But if the simulation model is huge (many resources, sources, trajectories...) and the time to instantiate it is a concern, then you can do this once and then reset() it for each iteration.

[1] https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-aa-5g
[2] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/discussions/244
[3] https://r-simmer.org/reference/reset.html
